daily.title: Syria: How  the 'house of sisters' threat split society
daily.summary: Rumor has it that the 'house of sisters' is where kidnapped women from other Syrian sects are forced to convert to Islam. Nobody knows if it really exists, but it's being used to create communal tensions anyway.

daily.title: LIV Golf in financial turmoil: what's next for the sport?
daily.summary: Six months after Saudi Arabia pulled funding from the breakaway organization, LIV Golf have filed for bankruptcy protection. Several of the world's best players signed on to LIV, so where does that leave golf?

daily.title: Norway's King Harald V laid to rest in state funeral
daily.summary: Heads of state from around the world came to Oslo to pay tribute to the late monarch.

daily.title: Serbia dissolves parliament as snap elections called
daily.summary: Serbia will head to the polls in late October after President Aleksandar Vucic dissolved parliament following growing pressure from protesters demanding political change. However, Vucic plans to stand as a PM candidate.

daily.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers, but not peace
daily.summary: Twenty-five years after 9/11, conspiracy theories about the terrorist attacks persist. But even as an attempt to make sense of a tragedy, psychologists say the benefit in conspiracy ideation or belief is short-lived.

daily.title: UK rules out cyberattack after major flight disruptions
daily.summary: Airports across the UK continue to face delays and cancellations after a flight processing system failure. The UK's transport secretary has summoned the CEO of National Air Traffic Services (NATS) for an explanation.

daily.title: The billion-euro trade driving Europe's eels to extinction
daily.summary: Traffickers are making big bucks smuggling millions of critically endangered eels across continents, using suitcases on planes and legal loopholes to deliver them to dinnerplates. Where are the smuggling hotspots?

daily.title: India: 5 baby orangutans rescued, smuggling suspected
daily.summary: Five young orangutans, not native to India, were found in an Odisha forest, sparking suspicion of an international smuggling operation. Meanwhile, India said it was not involved in the BAPS-Eiffel Tower row.

daily.title: Trafficked into fraud: An African crisis situation in Cambodia
daily.summary: Cambodia's crackdown on scam operators is stranding young African trafficking victims in the Asian country with no money, no passport and no prospects.

daily.title: Ukraine, Russia trade drone strikes, killing 6
daily.summary: At least four people were killed, and 29 others were injured, in a Ukrainian attack on a Russian Black Sea port. Meanwhile, Russian drones struck a crossing on the Ukraine-Moldova border, killing two.

daily.title: Germany news: Merz, Weidel face off after AfD state win
daily.summary: Alice Weidel and Friedrich Merz traded barbs the Bundestag days after the AfD's victory in Saxony-Anhalt has put new pressure on the German chancellor. DW has the latest.

daily.title: The Bayeux Tapestry in London: What's behind the hype?
daily.summary: The exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum is eagerly anticipated across the UK, as the medieval masterpiece is considered by many to be a symbol of the country's identity.

daily.title: EU sports commissioner says FIFA is 'damaging to football'
daily.summary: Speaking to DW, EU Commissioner Glenn Micallef hit out at world football's governing body over its "poor governance."

daily.title: BRICS leaders gather in India, but does the group have a clear purpose?
daily.summary: The 18th BRICS summit takes place in India this weekend. Unlike last year, the leaders of China and Russia are coming. But does the expanded group have a clear common mission and purpose?

daily.title: Putin rejects mobilization rumors, many Russians unconvinced
daily.summary: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has dismissed rumors about military mobilization. But many Russians, including many DW users, say they are preparing for the possibility.

daily.title: Dallas Republican convention: How Trump looms over midterms
daily.summary: Donald Trump is not on the ballot in the midterm elections — but the first Republican midterm convention is putting him center stage. It's a strategy that could prove risky for the party.

daily.title: Trump escalates trade war with Canada with import bans, 50% tariffs
daily.summary: US President Trump has announced new import bans and 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods as tensions between the two countries intensify. This comes a day after Ottawa's retaliatory tariffs on US products took effect.

daily.title: Israel's Netanyahu denies UAE warned him of October 7 attack
daily.summary: Israeli media reported that the UAE contacted Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu before the October 7, 2023 attacks, warning him that Hamas was planning a major operation. The prime minister has rejected the reports.

daily.title: US strikes oil tankers off coast of Iran
daily.summary: The US attacked four oil-carrying vessels in the Gulf of Oman and one in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it struck a US base in Jordan and ships trying to cross the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation.

daily.title: German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
daily.summary: The AfD won the election in the eastern German state by a wide margin. While politicians and election analysts are still debating the reasons for the far-right party's popularity, economists are sounding the alarm.

daily.title: Ratko Mladic’s funeral casts shadow over Bosnia and Herzegovina vote
daily.summary: Ratko Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade, attended by Serbian and Bosnian Serb leaders, has deepened regional tensions and could affect the upcoming election in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

daily.title: BSW and AfD – a political love-hate relationship in Germany
daily.summary: The Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) could help the Alternative for Germany (AfD) into power in Saxony-Anhalt. But the BSW is riddled with infighting

weekly.title: Afghanistan's women: A national soccer team without a home
weekly.summary: The Afghan women's national football team has finally been officially recognized by FIFA. Now the players want to make history both on and off the field.

weekly.title: PISA 2025 results: Reading and math scores plummet worldwide
weekly.summary: The PISA 2025 results reveal record-low student performance, with digital distractions and AI use raising concerns. Germany is faring worse than ever.

weekly.title: Elversberg: Bundesliga newcomers from tiny town make waves
weekly.summary: A team from a small southwestern German town of just 7,000 inhabitants made history by sealing promotion to become the 59th club to play in the Bundesliga. Elversberg has got off to a memorable start.

weekly.title: Female footballers offered egg freezing but doubts remain
weekly.summary: Spain's football federation are set to join a handful of clubs in paying for female players to freeze their eggs during their careers. While players have pushed for the move, there are welfare concerns too.

weekly.title: Werner Herzog: Germany's wild man of cinema is back
weekly.summary: As his latest movie, "Bucking Fastard," premiered at the Venice Film Festival, DW talked to the boundary-breaking director.

weekly.title: Nicaragua challenges German arms exports to Israel at ICJ
weekly.summary: Germany has asked the International Court of Justice to dismiss the case on jurisdiction grounds. It also said its arms exports to Israel were documented, published, and subject to more stringent checks than most.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt: Germany wakes up to 'unsettling' AfD victory
weekly.summary: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won the Saxony-Anhalt state election but without an absolute majority in parliament. Other European nations were wrestling with the impact of the results. Follow DW.

weekly.title: AfD wants to form a government in Saxony-Anhalt — but how?
weekly.summary: Following its record election success, the far-right Alternative for Germany aims to form a government. What options does it have without the absolute majority?

weekly.title: War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
weekly.summary: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election.

weekly.title: Chancellor Merz says AfD result 'changes all of Germany'
weekly.summary: A visibly shaken but also determined Friedrich Merz spoke in Berlin about the AfD's election victory in Saxony-Anhalt and the CDU's bitter defeat. He insisted on sticking to his reforms.

weekly.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
weekly.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt: Digesting the AfD's landmark election win
weekly.summary: With well over 40% for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), Saxony-Anhalt has witnessed a landmark election night. DW's reporters were on the ground.

weekly.title: Fact check: Election fraud claims spread in Saxony-Anhalt
weekly.summary: False and misleading claims are raising questions about the integrity of the election in Saxony-Anhalt. DW Fact Check takes a closer look.

weekly.title: Germany set to feel the impact of Saxony-Anhalt's AfD win
weekly.summary: The state election could have major consequences for Germany's government. Pollsters cite dissatisfaction with Merz as one reason for the CDU's poor showing.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt election: Why the AfD is so strong
weekly.summary: The AfD has emerged as the strongest party in Germany's eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt by a wide margin. What is driving support for the far right in this predominantly rural eastern German state?

weekly.title: Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
weekly.summary: Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease and its vectors.

weekly.title: Germany plans anti-drone shield over Leipzig attack — report
weekly.summary: Several German cities will receive rapidly deployable units capable of defending against drone strikes on critical infrastructure, according to Bild am Sonntag newspaper.

weekly.title: Hungary begins hunt for corrupt regime's billions
weekly.summary: Hungary's new prime minister promised he would recover billions stolen or diverted by the previous administration. A new "super authority" is about to begin that work. Its success or failure will have a big impact.

weekly.title: Croatia: Toxic waste protest draws tens of thousands
weekly.summary: The Zagreb demonstrators demanded that the government come up with a plan to clear illegal toxic waste in 20 days. Prime Minister Plenkovic has promised to tackle the issue.

weekly.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination
weekly.summary: Migration is a sensitive topic in Germany, with public debate dominated by the fear of uncontrolled immigration. But over two centuries, millions of Germans emigrated in search of a better life.

weekly.title: Germany news: Thousands march at Saxony-Anhalt rallies
weekly.summary: Ahead of Saxony-Anhalt's state election on Sunday, a democracy festival by civil society groups has been held in Magdeburg. The far-right AfD organized its final campaign rally in the state capital.

weekly.title: What would an AfD government in Saxony-Anhalt really mean?
weekly.summary: Detention centers for deportation, mandatory work for asylum-seekers, vigilante groups — the AfD wants to drastically overhaul Saxony-Anhalt. What does the party have planned?

weekly.title: Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder
weekly.summary: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity to murder journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Almost nine years after the attack, the question of who ordered her death remains unanswered.

weekly.title: In Saxony-Anhalt election, small parties will be kingmakers
weekly.summary: The far-right AfD has good odds of winning an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's parliament this state election, enabling them to govern alone. It all depends on whether other parties make the cut.

weekly.title: Germany's civil society alliance takes on the far right
weekly.summary: Trade unions, churches and human rights activists are worried about the rise of the far-right AfD. How can civil society protect people who are threatened by far-right extremism?

weekly.title: How vulnerable is Germany's infrastructure?
weekly.summary: The growing number of attacks on substations and railway lines in Germany is raising concern. Experts say that people will have to get used to the likelihood that such incidents will continue.

weekly.title: Majority of Germans see Russia as a threat
weekly.summary: More than half of German citizens believe that Germany's security is threatened by Russia, according to the latest survey by public broadcaster ARD.

weekly.title: The hidden environmental cost of AI data centers
weekly.summary: As data centers multiply to meet AI demand, they're straining power grids, draining water supplies and reshaping the land and air around them.

weekly.title: Serbia: How the funeral of Ratko Mladic is dividing a nation
weekly.summary: As the Serbian government leaves the decision about Ratko Mladic's funeral arrangements to his family, international pressure on the country is mounting. How do Serbs feel about the matter?

weekly.title: Germany: Is Saxony-Anhalt's economy really struggling?
weekly.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party has long claimed that the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt has been left behind. Is that really the case? A closer look at the data offers some interesting insights.

weekly.title: Why North Korea's women's football team is so good
weekly.summary: North Korea's young footballers enter the U-20 World Cup in Poland as defending champions — the 2024 title was their third. Why is the isolated state so good at the game?

weekly.title: 2026 Beethoven Festival evokes a sense of home
weekly.summary: The motto of this year's classical music festival in Bonn is "Home/At Home," featuring musicians from diverse cultures presenting pieces from their homelands.

weekly.title: How Volkswagen's huge workforce became a costly burden
weekly.summary: The struggling German carmaker plans to cut up to 100,000 jobs from its 630,000-strong workforce. How did VW's headcount get so bloated, and will the cuts be enough to survive the Chinese EV onslaught?

weekly.title: Berlin: BER Airport Terminal 1 reopened after security scare
weekly.summary: Police have given the all-clear at Terminal 1 at Berlin's BER Airport following an earlier security scare and evacuation. The airport said some flights had been delayed but they were trying to avoid any cancelations.

weekly.title: Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
weekly.summary: Authorities in Norway have seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, on a court order sought and obtained by Naftogaz in Ukraine. Russia has protested the move, which stems from its refusal to pay Naftogaz damages.

weekly.title: Is Germany's economic slump finally over?
weekly.summary: Despite a slew of negative headlines, the German economy has posted its best figures in years. There are reasons for optimism, but structural issues remain.

weekly.title: Macron visits Bayeux Tapestry with King Charles, PM Andy Burnham
weekly.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is on a shorter-term visit to the UK than the renowned on-loan 11th century tapestry. He viewed the ancient artwork with the UK monarch and relatively new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

weekly.title: Austria women ice hockey team fight for future generations
weekly.summary: Austria are getting ready for their first Women's Ice Hockey World Championship. But preparations have been overshadowed by a dispute about conditions, pay and getting men's cast-off kit. A solution now looks in sight.
